prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: first visual concept, simulated gameplay screenshot for a proposed Godot game.
Create a landscape 16:9 screenshot mockup of a 2D top-down pixel-art real-time one-versus-one arena fighting game set in Fullmetal Alchemist. This is a gameplay view, not a poster. Authentic crisp hand-crafted pixel art, limited colors, clear pixel clusters, no smooth painting or 3D rendering. Orthographic overhead view in the style of readable top-down 16-bit action games; visible tops and fronts of characters, NOT isometric and NOT side-scrolling.
Scene: a stone-paved Amestris military courtyard with perimeter brick walls, a few crates and ruined columns. Broad playable arena occupies most of the frame; small fighters with ample room to move and aim.
Exactly two active combatants: Edward Elric, recognizable blond braid, red coat and metallic automail arm, on left-center; Alphonse Elric, recognizable tall bulky gray suit of armor, on right-center. Edward is transmuting the floor into a jagged rising stone barrier with cyan alchemical sparks and a glowing ground transmutation effect. Alphonse is advancing with a transmuted stone spear, dust and cracked tiles showing terrain interaction. Clear silhouettes, grounded shadows, deliberate attack telegraph on the floor and a subtle dotted aiming line indicating real-time targeting. Effects must leave fighters readable.
Minimal polished game HUD: upper left a small Edward portrait, health bar and exact text "EDWARD"; upper right Alphonse portrait, health bar and exact text "ALPHONSE"; centered timer "01:28". Along bottom, four small pixel-art ability icons for metal blade, earth wall, stone spikes, and dash, with keyboard hints "Q", "W", "E", "SPACE". Thin dark charcoal HUD with brass trim, restrained cyan alchemy accents. Warm muted stone environment contrasts with red coat and cool armor. No Pokémon, no extra active fighters, no logos, no giant title, no decorative poster text. Make it feel like a plausible playable MVP screenshot with compelling terrain-changing combat.
